LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_d: The noiseless identity channel on a finite nonempty alphabet A has capacity ln |A| nats per use.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_c: A channel on finite alphabets whose output has the same law r for every input has capacity zero when the input alphabet is nonempty.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_channe: For a binary symmetric channel with crossover probability 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 and any input law, I(X;Y) = H(Y) − h(ε), where h is binary entropy in nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_b: The capacity of the binary symmetric channel with crossover probability 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 is ln 2 − h(ε) nats per use, where h is binary entropy in nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_channe: For every crossover probability 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1, a uniform binary input attains the capacity of the binary symmetric channel.
For a binary erasure channel with erasure probability 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 and any input law p, the mutual information between input and output is (1 − ε)H(p).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_b: The binary erasure channel with erasure probability 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 has capacity (1 − ε) ln 2 nats per use.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_d: Measured in bits per use, the capacity of the noiseless identity channel on a finite nonempty alphabet A is log₂ |A|.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_c: For finite alphabets and a nonempty input alphabet, a channel whose output law is independent of its input has capacity zero bits per use.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_b: The binary symmetric channel with crossover probability 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 has capacity 1 − h₂(ε) bits per use, where h₂ is binary entropy in bits.
The binary erasure channel with erasure probability 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 has capacity 1 − ε bits per use.
